description: BTech Data Science student working on the “Harmonization of MODIS and VIIRS Hot Spots” challenge. We will use NASA FIRMS data and Python to match fire detections from both satellites and build a harmonized dataset with maps and charts. Looking for teammates with skills in data analysis, visualization, Earth science, coding, or writing/design for the presentation. Beginners welcome. Deadline is tomorrow, so we will work fast and keep it simple. Hindi and English speakers welcome!
summary:
Ember Calendar is a Streamlit web application that harmonizes NASA FIRMS active-fire hotspot records from MODIS (Terra/Aqua, 2000–present) and VIIRS (Suomi NPP, 2012–present) into a consistent monthly burning-activity calendar on a 0.25° grid. It addresses sensor incompatibility through quality filtering, local-time monthly aggregation, and per-cell overlap calibration, producing comparable fire cell-days and raw detection metrics across the full record.
For a selected area of interest and date range, users can view a year-by-month burning calendar heatmap, compare a chosen month to its historical median to detect anomalies and critical periods, and download filtered CSV data. By uniting two decades of MODIS history with higher-detail VIIRS continuity, Ember Calendar helps emergency responders, scientists, and land managers recognize seasonal patterns and unusual burning. The deployed demo covers Argentina (Nov 2000–Oct 2026) using real NASA FIRMS data.
Source code: https://github.com/Ritika-Bhati-2266/Harmonization-of-MODIS-and-VIIRS-Hot-Spots
details:
What it does & how it works

Ember Calendar is a Streamlit web application that harmonizes NASA FIRMS active-fire hotspot records from MODIS (Terra/Aqua, 2000–present, Collection 6.1) and VIIRS (Suomi NPP, 2012–present, 375 m) into one consistent monthly burning-activity series on a 0.25° grid. Our reproducible Python pipeline (harmonize.py) quality-filters detections (MODIS confidence ≥ 30; VIIRS nominal/high), assigns them to grid cells with optional local-time month adjustment, and aggregates two metrics per cell-month-sensor: fire cell-days (platform-independent, deduplicated) and raw detections. On the 2012–2026 overlap, it estimates per-cell VIIRS→MODIS calibration ratios (shrunk toward a global ratio and clipped to 0.1–3.0) for each metric, then builds a continuous series using MODIS as the reference and calibrated VIIRS to fill gaps and extend the record. The app lets users draw or enter an area of interest, select a date range and month, and view a year×month heatmap, the selected month versus its historical median (anomaly %), annual trends, calibration reliability, and download filtered CSVs.

Bundled demo (Argentina)

Nov 2000–Oct 2026 (UTC−3) using real NASA FIRMS data: 4,373,521 quality-filtered detections across 4,221 cells and 301,741 cell-months. Cell-day overlap ratio 0.489 (R² 0.597), with 99% of cells using cell-specific calibration.

Benefits & intended impact

Ember Calendar gives early-warning responders, scientists, and land managers a fast, consistent view of peak fire seasons, exceptional years, and unusual burning months for any selected area, supporting monitoring, preparedness, and response.

Tools, languages & software

Python 3, Streamlit, pandas, NumPy, Plotly, Folium/streamlit-folium, Matplotlib, PyArrow (Parquet); GitHub and GitHub Actions (testing/CI); deployed on Render.

Creativity & factors considered

We combined dual calibrated metrics, auditable per-row calibration (ratios, overlap months, cell/global basis, source), local-time handling, and accessible color ramps (cividis). We prioritized comparability across sensors, reproducibility, transparency, and usability, while clearly documenting limitations (detections/cell-days ≠ burned area, partial latest months, and lower confidence for global-fallback cells).

Source code: https://github.com/Ritika-Bhati-2266/Harmonization-of-MODIS-and-VIIRS-Hot-Spots
